sentences.text:
JUDGMENT New India Assurance Company Limited has preferred these appeals challenging the judgment and award dated 06th October, 2015 passed in MVC Nos.1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 of 2014 on the file of Motor Accident Claims Tribunal Honnavar, (for short hereinafter referred to as the "Tribunal").
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties in these appeals are referred to as per their status and rank before the Tribunal.
3.

entities.text: JUDGMENT New India Assurance Company Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The brief facts of the case are that on 19th Nay, 2013, petitioners were travelling in a Toyata Qualis bearing Registration No.KA-30/M-2479 to Nippani via Belgaum from Honnavara.

at about 3.00 pm when the said vehicle was moving on National Highway-4 on Belagavi-Nippani Road near Kanagal Cross within the limits of Hukkeri Taluk, the driver of the said vehicle drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and lost control over the vehicle and dashed to the ongoing Lorry bearing registration No.TN-39/BH-3999 the inmates of the vehicle sustained grievous injuries and two of them died on the spot.

It is contended in the claim petitions that Respondent - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:14841-DB C/W MFA No. 101567 of 2016, MFA No. 101568 of 2016, MFA No.
101569 of 2016, No.3 is owner of truck bearing registration No.TN-39/BH-3999 and respondents 2 and 3 are owner and insurer of the Toyota Qualis vehicle respectively are liable to pay compensation and sought for compensation.

sentences.text: In pursuance of notice, Respondent No.3 has not appeared and Respondents 1, 2 and 4 have appeared and filed their statement of objections.
The substance of objection of respondent No.1 is that the accident has not occurred due to rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of Toyota Qualis.
The lorry bearing registration No.TN-39/BH-3999 was proceeding in front of Qualis, the driver of the lorry stopped the lorry without giving any signal.
Though the driver of Qualis tried to avoid the accident, but he could not.
Hence, the accident occurred due to negligent act on the part of the driver of the lorry.
The driver of the lorry has filed false case against the driver of Qualis.

The driver of the Qualis was having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and the vehicle was insured and the driver has not violated any terms and conditions of the policy and denied all other averments - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:14841-DB C/W MFA No. 101567 of 2016, MFA No. 101568 of 2016, MFA No.
101569 of 2016, made in the petition and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.

5. The substance of statement of objections of respondent No.2 is that the driver of the lorry has suddenly stopped the vehicle without giving any signal and because of the negligent act of the driver of the lorry the accident occurred.
It is also admitted that the car of the respondent No.1 was insured with the respondent No.2 Insurance Company and the driver of the Qualis vehicle was not having valid licence to drive the same.
Accordingly, respondent No.1 has violated the terms of policy.
On all these grounds sought to dismiss the claim petitions.
6. The substance of the statement of objections of respondent No.4 is that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of Quails vehicle.
It is admitted that the lorry was insured with respondent No.4- Insurance company.

It is further contended that the driver of the lorry was not having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and further denied the averments made - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:14841-DB C/W MFA No. 101567 of 2016, MFA No. 101568 of 2016, MFA No.
101569 of 2016, in the claim petition.
On all these grounds sought to dismiss the claim petitions.

In MVCs No.1, 2 and 6 of 2014:
1. 2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?, if so, what amount?
3. What order and award?
In MVC No.3 of 2014:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Mohammed Abban @ Abbas being inmate of the Qualis vehicle bearing No.KA-30/M-2479 - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:14841-DB C/W MFA No. 101567 of 2016, MFA No. 101568 of 2016, MFA No.

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount?

10. In view of the aforesaid findings, the Tribunal allowed the petitions in part awarded compensation of Rs.4,25,500/-; Rs.1,11,100/-; Rs.1,80,000/-; Rs.60,60,000/-; and Rs.62,300/-
respectively in MVCs No.1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 of - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:14841-DB C/W MFA No. 101567 of 2016, MFA No. 101568 of 2016, MFA No.
101569 of 2016, 2014.
Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award, insurance has preferred these appeals.

11. Sri R.R. Mane, learned counsel appearing for the appellant-Insurance Company submits that the Tribunal has failed to appreciate that the claimants in the claim petitions have mainly alleged that the driver of the Qualis vehicle has driven the said vehicle in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the ongoing lorry bearing registration No.TN-39/BH- 3999 from behind and subsequently introduced a theory in their evidence that the driver of the said lorry suddenly stopped the lorry on the road without giving any indication and that the driver of the Qualis also falsely made out a similar case, only to avoid liability.

The documentary evidence available on record such as FIR,
complaint, charge sheet, spot sketch and panchnama were produced by the claimants coupled with oral evidence of the driver of the lorry, clearly falsify the contention of the claimants and the driver and owner of the Quails vehicle.

The learned counsel submitted that the driver of the lorry was driving the vehicle in a moderate speed and with all caution, but it is the driver of the Qualis vehicle who drove the said - 17 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:14841-DB C/W MFA No. 101567 of 2016, MFA No. 101568 of 2016, MFA No.
101569 of 2016, vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the lorry from behind.

The learned counsel further submits that the Tribunal also failed to appreciate that after investigation,
the police authorities have filed charge sheet against the driver of the Qualis vehicle.
He also submits that the Judgment and Award passed by the Tribunal is contrary to law and facts of the case.
The learned counsel also submits that that the Tribunal has erred in awarding interest at the rate of 8% per annum, which is on the higher side.
On all these grounds, the learned counsel sought to allow the appeals.

12. On the other hand, learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondents, support the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal and submit that the Tribunal, based on the oral and documentary evidence, has allowed the claims petitions in part and awarded just and proper compensation, which cannot be interfered in these appeals and hence sought to dismiss the appeals.

Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and having perused the material on record, the following points arise for our consideration in these appeals:
- 18 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:14841-DB C/W MFA No. 101567 of 2016, MFA No. 101568 of 2016,
MFA No. 101569 of 2016,
1.

Whether the appellant-Insurance Company has made out a ground in all these appeals to interfere with the finding given by the Tribunal as to rash and negligent act on the part of drivers of both the vehicles viz. Qualis bearing Registration No.KA-30/M-2479 and Lorry bearing Registration No.TN-39/BH-3999?
2. Whether the appellant-Insurance Company has made out a ground to reduce the interest rate from 8% per annum as awarded by the Tribunal to 6% per annum?
3. What order or award?
15. We have carefully examined the materials placed before this Court.

On the basis of the complaint filed by one Balamurugan the driver of lorry bearing registration No.TN- 39/BH-3999 against the driver of the Toyota Qualis vehicle bearing registration No.KA-30/M-2749, the case came to be registered for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337,
- 19 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:14841-DB C/W MFA No. 101567 of 2016, MFA No. 101568 of 2016, MFA No.
101569 of 2016, 338 and 304A of the Indian Penal Code and the Investigating Officer conducted spot mahazar and recorded the statement of eye-witnesses, obtained postmortem report and submitted the charge sheet.

Based on the materials on record, the Tribunal has elaborately appreciated the evidence adduced by PWs.1 to 5 and also the evidence adduced on behalf of respondents 1 to 3 and also upon examination of documents which were marked as Exhibits R1 to 6,
and also relying upon the decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of KHEYNEI v. NEW INDIA ASSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED AND OTHERS reported in 2015 ACJ 1441, has held that the drivers of both the Lorry and the Toyata Qualis vehicles have equally contributed to the accident in question in the ratio of 50:50.

sentences.text: On re-appreciation/re-examination of the entire material placed on record, we do not find any legal infirmities/illegalities in the finding given by the Tribunal.
Hence, there is no ground to interfere with the impugned Judgment and Award as to the liability of the Insurance Company, as determined by the Tribunal.
Accordingly, we answer point No.1 in the negative.
As regards the awarding of the interest on the compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has awarded interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till realisation.
The accident took place in the year 2014.

Considering the rate of interest on fixed deposits in the Nationalised Banks the interest rate awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side and the same is to be reduced to 6% per annum, which would be just and reasonable.
Hence, we answer, point No.2, partly in the affirmative.

The Judgment and Award dated 06th October, 2015 passed in MVC No.1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 of 2014 is modified by reducing the interest rate to 6% per annum as against rate of 8% per annum, awarded by the Tribunal.

In pursuance of notice, Respondent No.3 has not appeared and Respondents 1, 2 and 4 have appeared and filed their statement of objections.
The substance of objection of respondent No.1 is that the accident has not occurred due to rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of Toyota Qualis.
The lorry bearing registration No.TN-39/BH-3999 was proceeding in front of Qualis, the driver of the lorry stopped the lorry without giving any signal.
Hence, the accident occurred due to negligent act on the part of the driver of the lorry.
The driver of the lorry has filed false case against the driver of Qualis.
The driver of the Qualis was having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and the vehicle was insured and the driver has not violated any terms and conditions of the policy and denied all other averments - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:14841-DB C/W MFA No. 101567 of 2016, MFA No. 101568 of 2016, MFA No.

In MVCs No.1, 2 and 6 of 2014:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that she being inmate of the Qualis vehicle bearing No.KA- 30/M-2479 has sustained bodily injuries in the accident that took place on 19.05.2013 at about 15.00 hours near Kanagala Cross on NH-4, involving the said Qualis vehicle and lorry bearing New India Assurance Co.Ltd vs Rahina Kousar on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185089101/

3. What order and award?

opennyai_summary.arguments:
The documentary evidence available on record such as FIR,
complaint, charge sheet, spot sketch and panchnama were produced by the claimants coupled with oral evidence of the driver of the lorry, clearly falsify the contention of the claimants and the driver and owner of the Quails vehicle.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
New India Assurance Co.Ltd vs Rahina Kousar on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185089101/
13 16.
On re-appreciation/re-examination of the entire material placed on record, we do not find any legal infirmities/illegalities in the finding given by the Tribunal.
Hence, there is no ground to interfere with the impugned Judgment and Award as to the liability of the Insurance Company, as determined by the Tribunal.
As regards the awarding of the interest on the compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has awarded interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till realisation.
The accident took place in the year 2014.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Considering the rate of interest on fixed deposits in the Nationalised Banks the interest rate awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side and the same is to be reduced to 6% per annum, which would be just and reasonable.
Hence, we answer, point No.2, partly in the affirmative.
18. For the aforesaid reasons, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER 1. Appeals are allowed in part;
2.
The Judgment and Award dated 06th October, 2015 passed in MVC No.1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 of 2014 is modified by reducing the interest rate to 6% per annum as against rate of 8% per annum, awarded by the Tribunal.
